Have you ever noticed how some months have 30 days, some have 31 and somehow one has 28, sometimes 29?

Well, that's pretty confusing.

Since the Earth takes about 365 days to go around the Sun once, either we make our seconds longer, which we can't, or we start using a different monthly and weekly division.

I thought of two ways of doing that:

  • Since 365=5x73, we could divide the year into 5 73-day "months" or "seasons", adding a day to the last month following the current scheme.
    We'll then group every 12 days into a week, making the month 6 weeks long, with one last vacational day (73 might also be a cool number but it's a prime) [first system];     (discarded)
  • Since 365=28x13+1, we could divide the year into 12 28-day months and one 29 days long, to which we'll eventually add a day following the current scheme.
    Each month will be divided into 4 7-day weeks, keeping the current names for the days of the week and changing a bit the names of the months so that their names finally match their number (naming system partially reddit.com/u/xenodit's idea)[second system]:
1 2 3 4 5 6
Henember Dicember Tricember Tetramber Pentamber Hexamber
7 8 9 10 11 12 13
Heptamber Octo(m)ber Ennamber Decamber Hendecamber Dodecamber Triskamber.

I personally like the second system better.
